brief.headline: Roman has had a fall (Oct 19), new evening confusion (Nov 9), a drop in weight of about 9% since Sep 5, and a decline in bathing and dressing ability since Sep 18, so the team should review these together.

items.statement: On Nov 9, 2026 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. He was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The RN planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. The notes provided do not show results or a visit after that.
items.verifier_note: The clinical details match the Nov 9 note. The cited note names only "Linda" and doesn't say she is his niece. That relationship appears in a different note, not in this citation.

items.statement: Roman fell at home in the kitchen on Oct 19, 2026 while reaching for a cabinet, and Linda found him on the floor. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness. He had a small skin tear on his left forearm. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. No ED or hospital encounter is recorded.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 19 nursing note matches every detail. The encounters record is empty, so "no ED or hospital encounter" is accurate.

items.statement: PT evaluated him on Oct 24, 2026 and found his gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use. His Timed Up and Go was 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see him twice weekly. The notes do not show whether any of the equipment or the home evaluation is in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation matches all details: gait, cane use, TUG 19 seconds, the three recommendations and twice-weekly visits. The statement doesn't claim any equipment is in place.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on Sep 5 to 75.2 kg on Nov 24, 2026, a loss of 7.1 kg (8.6%). The readings were 79.8 kg on Oct 1 and 77.3 kg on Oct 28. On Nov 24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record has all four weights and the -7.1 kg / -8.6% change. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast, 50% lunch and plan details. The note rounds the loss to 9%, which is consistent.

items.statement: On Sep 18, 2026 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting him out of the tub, and he said he had been skipping showers for fear of slipping. On Sep 25 the OT found he needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, where he was independent at the last review. The OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing. The notes do not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 18 aide note and Sep 25 OT note match all details, including the change from independent at last review and the three recommendations.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on Nov 9 completed, and what did they show about the evening confusion?
Could the weight loss, new confusion and fall be related, and who is coordinating the work-up?
Which of the OT and PT equipment and home changes (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, front-wheeled walker, grab bars, home safety evaluation) are in place, and have home care hours been increased?
Is the kitchen and stove safe while he is more confused in the evenings, and what support does Linda need?
The medication list still shows naproxen sodium alongside clopidogrel, and he has recorded anemia and weight loss. Should this be covered in the medication review?

checks: Confirm review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and enrollment context (enrolled 2024-10-07); identify what changed since the last IDT review.

Falls and near-falls in window: count, circumstances, injuries, and any fall-related ED visit or admission; check fall-risk screening and home safety items given knee osteoarthritis, chronic pain, and fibromyalgia.

ED visits and hospital admissions in window: reasons, discharge summaries, and whether follow-up appointments occurred. Pay particular attention to any cardiac (ischemic heart disease) or COPD/bronchitis exacerbation presentations.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, naproxen, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) against any starts or stops in window; flag any new prescriptions, dose changes, or discontinuations, and any PRN nitroglycerin use.

Bleeding and GI risk review: naproxen (NSAID) taken alongside clopidogrel with anemia on problem list; check hemoglobin/CBC trend, reports of melena, bruising, or bleeding, and whether the NSAID use has been reviewed by the prescriber.

Cardiovascular and blood pressure trend: BP readings in window against hypertension history; heart rate trend on beta-blocker; chest pain or angina reports; lipid panel status on simvastatin 20 mg if due.

Respiratory status: inhaler or bronchodilator use (none listed as active, so confirm whether medications are managed elsewhere), oxygen use, dyspnea, sputum changes, and recent pulmonary function or vaccination items if due.
Metabolic and weight trend: weight and BMI (obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes) over window; check glucose or HbA1c results and whether repeat testing is due.

Pain management: chronic pain, low back pain, knee osteoarthritis, and fibromyalgia scores; pain-related function limits; whether non-drug or non-NSAID options were discussed; any new analgesic requests.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, mobility aids, meal preparation, medication management, and driving or transport in window; compare to last assessment.

Cognition, mood, and engagement: cognitive screen results if due, depression or anxiety screen (chronic pain and multiple chronic conditions raise risk), sleep, and attendance at PACE center or day programming.

Caregiver and social situation: living arrangement changes, caregiver strain or availability, transportation barriers, and any housing or financial concerns from Kingsburg residence; document updates.

Care-plan items due in window: check dates for care-plan review, provider visits, labs, immunizations, eye and foot exams for prediabetes, and any open IDT action items from the last meeting; list overdue items for the team.
